Subject: GPU pool topology choices + burst policy check-ins (Atlas Health dedicated)

Hi Elena / team —

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. Per our MPP, next up is nailing the pool topology decision and the autoscale/burst policy so Ops can provision the dedicated capacity without rework. To keep the implementation sprint tight we need a few decisions from your side by EOD Monday:

1) Regional anchor: confirm primary region (us-west1 or us-east4). This determines network egress and where we'll place the warm warmers for burst.
2) Pool sizing: do you want a single large homogeneous pool (N1: 16xA100-equivalent) or a split pool topology (steady-state small pool + burst pool)? I included pros/cons in the attached atlas_onboard_requirements.pdf.
3) Burst SLAs: confirm whether 99th-percentile latency SLO is more important than burst cost — we can set burst headroom to 25% (default), 50% (aggressive), or adaptive (cost-aware). See burst_policy_matrix.xlsx.

Quick notes:
- If you pick split pools we can reserve a smaller steady pool for critical traffic and allow the burst pool to scale on preemptible instances for cost savings.
- Network topology (attached) shows our preferred VPC peering / Private Service Connect layout for us-west1.

Proposal: 30-min decision sync Thursday 10/18 11:00 PT to confirm choices and sign off on the MOP. If that works, I’ll loop in NetOps and the provisioning lead.

Attachments: atlas_onboard_requirements.pdf (decision matrix), burst_policy_matrix.xlsx, network_topology_diagram.png

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior CS Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Elena Rivas <elena@atlashealth.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.ai>, Samir Joshi <samir.j@cloudops.com>
Date: 2029-10-17T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GPU pool topology choices + burst policy check-ins (Atlas Health dedicated)

Vivek —

Thanks for the clear write-up. Quick answers from our side so you can proceed with the draft MOP:

1) Primary region: us-east4 (closer to our analytics cluster and regulatory gateway).
2) Pool sizing: leaning toward split pools — steady pool sized for predictable transactional traffic, burst pool for nightly batch inference. Cost is important but we can accept slightly higher steady cost for latency guarantees.
3) Burst SLA posture: choose 50% headroom for the first 60 days, then revisit once we have traffic telemetry.

We can do the 10/18 11:00 PT sync. Samir from CloudOps will join to discuss peering and router reachability. Procurement is looping to start the invoicing path once the MOP and SOW are locked.

—Elena
VP Product, Atlas Health
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-10-17T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: RE: GPU pool topology choices + burst policy check-ins (Atlas Health dedicated)

All —

Thanks Elena, that clarifies the high level. Quick ops notes for the 10/18 sync so we have a target MOP draft to iterate on:

- Provisioning plan: I’ll create a two-pool topology in the staging project (steady: 8xA100-eq; burst: 24xA100-eq preemptible-backed). If legal/regulatory needs require dedicated non-preemptible for burst we’ll flag it.
- Autoscale: we recommend the following baseline policy (we'll review live):
  • Steady pool: target CPU util 60%-70% with lower-bound of 6 nodes (safety).
  • Burst pool: scale immediately on queue depth with a 30s scale-up window and 5m cooldown. Headroom set to 50% initially.
- Warmers: We'll keep 2 warmers in the same region as the steady pool for instant KV cache priming.
- Observability: will ship a telemetry dashboard and a synthetic test set to track P99 latency and token throughput.

I attached an early version of the burst matrix for the call. Please review, especially the P99 vs cost trade column.

Ben
Provisioning Lead, Redwood Inference

Great sync this morning — notes and next steps below. I’m attaching the finalized burst_policy_matrix.xlsx and a lightweight runbook snippet we will use for the first 30 days.

Decisions made (recap):
- Region: us-east4 confirmed.
- Topology: split pools approved (steady 8 nodes non-preemptible, burst 24 nodes preemptible).
- Burst headroom: 50% for first 60 days; automated rollback to 25% if we exceed the monthly cost threshold that Elena’s team set (see drive link).

Action items:
- Ben: provision staging topology and hand network diagrams to Samir by EOD 10/19.
- Olga: generate access list and service account docs for Atlas engineers.
- Monica: start the SOW redline loop with Procurement; include the 60-day revisit clause and conditional scaling rollback.
- Vivek: schedule the first post-turnup telemetry review for 11/08 and confirm synthetic test set with Atlas.
